task_description: Write a method in Dafny to remove all elements from a given integer array present in another integer array.
specification_response:
Method Signature:
    method RemoveElements(mainArray: array<int>, removeArray: array<int>) returns (result: array<int>)
Postconditions_prompt:
    - The result array should contain all elements from mainArray that are not present in removeArray
- The result array should not contain any elements that are in removeArray
- The order of elements in the result array should preserve the order from mainArray for elements not removed
code_response:
Step 1: Determine the method’s signature.
In this case:
    method RemoveElements(s: array<int>, toRemove: array<int>) returns (result: seq<int>)
    
Step 2: Determine the preconditions.
In this case:
Natural language description:
    - Both input arrays should be non-null
    
Dafny specification:
    requires s != null
    requires toRemove != null
    
Step 3: Determine the postconditions.
In this case:
Natural language description:
    - The result sequence contains all elements from s that are not present in toRemove
    - The result sequence contains no elements present in toRemove
    - The order of remaining elements in s is preserved in the result
    
Dafny specification:
    ensures forall x :: x in result ==> !(x in toRemove)
    ensures forall x :: x in s ==> (x in result) <==> !(x in toRemove)
    ensures |result| == |filter(x | x in s && !(x in toRemove), s)|
    
(Note: Dafny sequences are immutable; the focus is on the final sequence content matching the criteria.)

Step 4: Write the code, its formal specification, and the verification annotations that help the solver prove the postconditions.
In this case:

```dafny
predicate InArray(arr: array<int>, x: int)
  reads arr
{
    exists i :: 0 <= i < arr.Length && arr[i] == x
}

method RemoveElements(s: array<int>, toRemove: array<int>) returns (result: seq<int>)
    requires s != null
    requires toRemove != null
    ensures forall x :: x in result ==> !(x in toRemove)
    ensures forall x :: x in s ==> (x in result) <==> !(x in toRemove)
{
    var res: seq<int> := [];
    var i := 0;
    while i < s.Length
        invariant 0 <= i <= s.Length
        invariant forall x :: x in res ==> !(x in toRemove)
        invariant forall x :: x in s[..i] ==> (x in res) <==> !(x in toRemove)
        decreases s.Length - i
    {
        if !InArray(toRemove, s[i]) && s[i] !in res
        {
            res := res + [s[i]];
        }
        i := i + 1;
    }
    result := res;
}
```
